result.title: Coverage-Verified Sparse Attention: Closed-Loop Quality Control for Long-Context LLM Decoding
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. 35 pages, 12 figures, 35 tables
result.summary: Sparse attention accelerates long-context decoding by reading a subset of the KV cache, but existing methods are open-loop: the kernel commits to its selection with no signal indicating whether enough attention mass was preserved and no recovery path when it was not. The needed signal already exists inside the kernel. The fraction of softmax mass on the selected tokens, which we call coverage, satisfies an exact algebraic equality with per-step output error and serves a dual role as the acceptance criterion and the interpolation weight for recovery. Coverage-Verified Sparse Attention (CVSA) turns coverage into a training-free, closed-loop verify-then-correct decode loop that accepts high-coverage drafts and recovers only the heads that fall short, with no sampling, no draft model, and no speculative-decoding infrastructure. Quality varies by only $0.14$ points across the threshold sweep; budget and scheduling ablations characterize the deployed operating point. On LongBench at 7B and 70B, CVSA comes within $1.13$ points of dense attention, statistically matching it at 70B, and it loses $0.8$ points on RULER; measured median decode-step speedup reaches $6.21\times$ at 128K context.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CVSA：把被选 token 上的 softmax 质量（coverage）作为与单步输出误差存在精确代数关系的信号，训练-free 地构成「验证—纠正」闭环稀疏注意力解码，仅对 coverage 不足的注意力头回退到稠密计算，在 7B/70B 上接近稠密注意力并取得显著解码加速。
AI.relevance_reason: coverage 作为「已选证据是否足够」的可度量信号，并兼作接受准则与插值权重，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选是否保留必要信息、以及 LOOK/STOP 式动态计算与停止决策提供可供核查的验证与纠正思路；但该工作为纯文本 KV 稀疏化，多模态迁移性需自行判断。
